title: Mode-tunable inter-core coupling of photon-number-resolved quantum light in a telecom multicore fiber
authors: Chiran Wijesundara, Yasmin Sarhan, Henry Strong, Jeffrey Cai, Dan T. Nguyen, Tim Thomay
abstract: Multicore optical fibers (MCFs), developed to scale classical telecommunications, are gaining traction as a quantum platform for high-dimensional key distribution, entanglement, and photonic quantum walks. So far, quantum light has occupied these fibers only as single-mode path channels; the spatial-mode structure within each core has remained untouched. Here we operate a telecom-grade 39-core fiber far from its design wavelength, where each core supports exactly two LP mode groups (LP01, LP11), and measure heralded photon-number states |1> and |2>, resolving the photon number simultaneously with the intra-core spatial mode or with the core index. Displacing the launch prepares a coherent LP01-LP11 superposition whose single-sided intensity pattern shows that the intermodal phase is preserved over the fiber: a drift-resolved joint fit gives a pixel asymmetry (0.4% vs 47%) incompatible with an incoherent mode mixture. Because the two modes couple to neighboring cores at different rates (kappa_LP11/kappa_LP01 = 2.4), the launched mode content acts as a state-selectable coupling knob: the effective inter-core coupling of the passive fiber is set by the launch alone (3.9-13.1%), a tunability that otherwise requires electro-optic, thermo-optic, or mechanical reconfiguration. The propagation is photon-number independent: the per-photon crosstalk of heralded |2> states equals that of |1>, bounding any Fock-state dependence to |dx/x| < 6.1% (95% CL), and the imaged mode distributions of |1> and |2> agree to better than 1%. This measured linear-optics null, validated against exact Fock-space simulation, is the baseline against which genuine multiphoton interference in fiber quantum walks must be certified; we also show how coincidence-based event selection produces spurious photon-number-dependent crosstalk if accidentals are not subtracted.
summary: The research demonstrates a novel quantum platform using multicore optical fibers to manipulate quantum light by controlling inter-core coupling using the launched spatial mode content. By resolving photon number and spatial modes simultaneously, the authors show that the coupling strength can be tuned without external hardware reconfiguration, establishing a robust, scalable tool for quantum information processing.
main_problem: To utilize multicore optical fibers as a quantum platform capable of simultaneously encoding and resolving multiple degrees of freedom: core index, intra-core spatial mode, and photon number.
main_result: The experiment demonstrates that the inter-core coupling can be actively tuned by controlling the launched spatial mode superposition, while maintaining a photon-number independent linear-optics null.
method: The authors use heralded photon-number states (|1> and |2>) generated via SPDC and measure the resulting spatial intensity patterns across the multicore fiber.
model_or_system: The platform is a telecom-grade 39-core multicore fiber, where each core supports two LP mode groups ($	ext{LP}_{01}, 	ext{LP}_{11}$). The system is analyzed using coupled-mode theory to model the coupling between cores and modes.
key_observables: Intermodal phase preservation, effective inter-core coupling strength (tunable via launch), and the degree of photon-number independence (crosstalk comparison between |1> and |2>).
important_parameters: Inter-core coupling range (3.9-13.1%), photon number resolution ($|1angle, |2angle$), and the coherence visibility ($V \ge 0.95$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that the measured intensity patterns are governed by a coherent superposition of modes, which is validated against exact Fock-space simulations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the 39-core fiber structure, the experimental setup using SPDC and photon-number-resolving heralds, and the spatial-mode coupling concept showing how launch content dictates coupling strength.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical system (MCFs with multiple modes), details the advanced measurement techniques (heralded photon number resolution), and presents the results showing mode-tunable coupling and photon-number independence, culminating in a validation against theoretical simulations.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly controllable, solid-state quantum channel where multiple degrees of freedom (core, mode, photon number) can be addressed independently, which is crucial for building scalable quantum networks and quantum simulation architectures.

Fig. 2 | Experimental setup (3D render). A frequency-doubled Ti:Sapphire regenerative amplifier pumps type-II SPDC in BBO. Idler photons pass a monochromator and a fiber-beam- splitter cascade onto four APDs, which together form the photon-number-resolving herald; signal photons are launched by a piezo-positioned single-mode fiber into the end-of-arc core of the multicore fiber, whose output facet is imaged onto the APD array (four read-out pixels). All eight detector channels share one time base. In the core-resolved configuration the pixels SE, C and NW+W collect cores 1, 2 and 3.
